components.name: Wrapped Slide Hero
components.description: Signature frame: label, one giant number (.slide-hero), exactly one roast line (the only friend dig is on Personality), --glow-hero behind. Built on .slide-container + .slide-stack so tall content scrolls instead of clipping; top spacer reserves 56px + notch inset. Tap zones: left third back, rest forward. One hedge per number: an estimate carries one "~" (read as "about") and no number is restated in the same frame. Top five leads with the top list share, or, with 5 or fewer different shows and movies, with that count (never "100%"). Biggest binge on date-only files holds at most five text elements: label, count, "titles in one day", the quip (never restating the count), and one footnote that defines a binge as one calendar day and names what was on. The intro offers a quiet "Skip to my card" on a re-watch, or "Skip to {group}" ("your group" past 24 characters) when a fresh invite waits; both jump to the card.

components.name: Share Card
components.description: Signature end frame: on-screen twin of the share PNG. Wordmark with a drawn play-triangle mark (white on screen, Reel Red in the PNG). White personality hero over one faint glow, roast line, divider, top-show punchline, one total. The red on slide 10 belongs to the CTA below (share, invite, or stack up), so the card adds none; the exported PNG alone fills the hero with the red gradient (exported images are exempt from The One Red Thing Rule). Invite actions have exactly three names: "Start my group and invite" (create; signed out, and while the session is still being read, it reads "Sign in and start my group", spelled with "and", never "&", and it only switches wording while neither focused nor pressed, so the label never changes under the thumb; sends share_teaser: true, disclosed by the one-line helper "Stats, never your file. Invites show your personality."), "Share my card and invite" (has a group), "Share my card" (no invite); "Share it now" is only the follow-up step after a create (also after the ?autoshare=1 sign-in return); under it the suggested group name (owner only) and nickname show as prefilled inline-editable fields ("Group name", "Your name"): Enter or blur saves (rename / nickname helpers), optimistically, Escape reverts, errors show inline under the field, and sharing is never blocked; "Share it now" accepts them as they are. A rename re-renders the card and PNG. A fresh pending invite (including ?join=CODE on /wrapped/{id}) means stack-up mode, checked before create; its CTA reads "See how you stack up in {group}" with the name shortened to "your group" past 24 characters. Create mode is distilled to card, one tease line, the red CTA, one disclosure line, and one secondary row: a "Join a friend's group" secondary button beside a quiet "Share my card"; "Upload a different file" is overflow (hidden on short screens and below md in create mode). "Card shared" with no group says "Now start a group?" and refocuses the CTA. With a group, a quiet "Open {group name}" link that becomes a secondary button after "Card shared". Empty reels show "Nothing to share yet" with an Upload CTA instead of group creation. A 422 on create says "Your stats couldn't be read. Upload your file again." Invite codes display uppercase everywhere, and share text carries the code plus the link. Only a 2xx group check confirms the code; 404 forgets the group; 401, 5xx, network failure or a check past 4s share without the code as "Share my card", and the stored group is kept (a late 2xx can still confirm it). A group from an older reel is kept, never cleared: its "Open {group}" link becomes a secondary "Update my stats in {group}" button. With a code, the card and PNG carry an invite block: an uppercase label "Join {group name}" ("Join my group" / "Join our group" when the name runs past 24 characters), the code as one mono chip (6px radius, Seat Row Raised, 1px Hairline, 0.2em tracking, the shared InviteCodeChip on screen), and the join link; no panel around it.

narrative.overview:
Autoplayed is a highlight reel that teases you. Every wrapped slide is one punchline: a single enormous number or word lands in the middle of a dark screening room, a red glow blooms behind it, and a line of copy delivers the joke. The reel exists to be screenshotted and dropped into the group chat, so each frame must read in a glance on a phone and still look good cropped.

The atmosphere is cinematic: near-black backgrounds, soft radial red light, glass panels that let the glow through. That glow is the brand's warmth and carries across the whole app, not just the slides. The rest of the interface stays quiet and dark so the hero always wins. Density is low and confident: big type, wide margins, one idea per screen.

The palette is Netflix-adjacent by choice, but Autoplayed is clearly unofficial: it never borrows the Netflix logo, wordmark, or "N" mark, and it says plainly that it is not affiliated.
keyCharacteristics: One hero per frame: a huge black-weight number or word, everything else steps back.
Cinematic red glow (radial gradients, soft halos) as the signature atmosphere.
Dark-only: a screening room, never a lit page.
Bold, punchy, teasing copy set big enough to screenshot.
Motion that lands like a reveal: hero pops in (or rises, wipes from the frame edge), context fades up after; the Personality verdict is stamped in with a swelling glow and a held beat.
A reel that ends on its verdict: Most loyal, then Personality, then the share card.
Scroll-safe frames: slides center when they fit and scroll from the top when they do not.
Every slide from 2 to 9 carries a small "Autoplayed · {host}" watermark so screenshots keep their attribution.

rules.name: The One Red Thing Rule
rules.body: Each screen has one red focal point: the primary action or the hero glow. If two things are red, one of them is wrong. On slide 10 the red is the CTA, so the on-screen share card's hero is white. Exported images are exempt: the share PNG carries no CTA, so its personality hero takes the red gradient.

rules.name: The Forced Colors Rule
rules.body: Transparent-fill text (.text-gradient-red) falls back to CanvasText under forced-colors: active so heroes never vanish.

rules.name: The Count The Notch Once Rule
rules.body: .slide-stack reserves 56px plus the top safe-area inset; the slide box never adds it again.

rules.name: The Two Taps To Leave Rule
rules.body: The X opens an inline confirm anchored to it; Escape and outside taps close only the popover, never the reel.

rules.name: The Small Red Text Rule
rules.body: Red text under 24px uses Reel Red, Text, never Reel Red. Reel Red fails contrast at body sizes.

rules.name: The Size Is The Joke Rule
rules.body: The punchline is carried by scale, not decoration. If a hero needs an icon or emoji to land, the number is not big enough.

rules.name: The Spotlight Rule
rules.body: Glow follows the hero. One glow source per frame, centered on the thing the frame is about; never glow on chrome like nav bars or inputs.

dos: Do give every wrapped slide exactly one hero stat at hero-stat size (or a named exception: Your week long hero, Personality climax), with the red glow centered behind it.
Do use Reel Red, Text (`#ff4d55`) for any red text under 24px.
Do keep the spring overshoot easing for hero pop-ins on slides only; UI chrome uses the smooth or out-expo easing.
Do mark estimated numbers with one "~" (one hedge per number) and a short Usher Grey note; never restate the same number twice in a frame or on the card.
Do keep a 44px minimum touch target on every control and a visible white focus ring.
Do say "not affiliated with Netflix" wherever the brand could be mistaken as official.
Do build slide columns with .slide-container plus .slide-stack so tall content scrolls instead of clipping.
Do use --glow-hero, --color-track and --color-track-strong instead of inline glows and bar fills.
Do use text-display, text-headline and text-title instead of arbitrary text sizes.
Do ask before leaving the reel; keep slide 10's red on the CTA.
donts: Don't use the Netflix logo, wordmark, or "N" mark anywhere.
Don't use gradient text on page headings; the red gradient belongs to slide hero stats only.
Don't put more than one glow source or more than one red focal point in a frame.
Don't use emoji as icons; use inline SVG.
Don't add uppercase eyebrow labels above page headlines; labels live on slides and stat cards.
Don't build rows of identical icon-plus-heading cards; use divided lists.
Don't introduce a light theme; the system is dark-only.
Don't add env(safe-area-inset-top) to a slide box; .slide-stack already reserves it.
Don't use justify-content: center on a slide column; it cuts off overflow above the fold.
